item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00258","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C16","C17","C04"],"selected_candidate_label":"C16","confidence":0.82,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C16 plausibly supplied the child’s core two-section drafting pattern: first designate a lead department to carry out functions under an act, then direct or request other federal agencies to assist that department in carrying out those responsibilities. The close sequence and corresponding language constitute more than generic delegation boilerplate. C17 closely resembles the child’s designation of one department to perform all statutory functions subject to exceptions and its supersession clause, while C04 is substantively related to federal exposition administration and assigns relevant functions to Commerce, but neither matches the child’s opening designation-plus-interagency-cooperation sequence as closely as C16.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Department of Commerce is hereby designated as the department to perform all functions provided for in the act except those functions which the act either authorizes other agencies to perform or vests, in terms, in the President.","parent_excerpt":"The Department of State is designated as the agency of the Government of the United States which shall, subject to the provisions of section 2 hereof, make or prepare the thorough investigations and written reports required by section 11 (a) of the said Refugee Relief Act of 1953","explanation":"Both begin by designating a particular department as the lead agency for carrying out functions required by a named act, subject to stated limitations."},{"child_excerpt":"Other interested departments and agencies of the Federal Government, including the Department of State and the National Science Foundation, are requested to cooperate ... with the Department of Commerce in carrying out the provisions of the act.","parent_excerpt":"The Department of the Army and such other agencies of the Government as the Department of State may request shall ... furnish the Department of State such assistance as it may need in carrying out its responsibilities under section 1 of this order.","explanation":"Both immediately follow the lead-agency designation with an interagency-assistance provision directing other federal entities to support the designated department in performing the statutory work."}]}
